extra.message: User input from request.GET['host'] is concatenated directly into a shell command passed to os.system() in course_shell_probe_701: _os.system("ping -c 1 " + host). extra.message: In course_bundle_thaw_185, attacker-controlled request body (or GET 'blob' parameter, optionally base64-decoded) is passed to pickle.loads(). A crafted pickle payload executes arbitrary Python code during deserialization, giving full remote code execution.

extra.message: In course_jinja_cast_683, the user-supplied GET parameter 'fragment' is concatenated into a jinja2 Template string that is then rendered: Template("Result: " + fragment).render(). This is a Server-Side Template Injection allowing execution of arbitrary Python expressions (e.g. {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }}) and remote code execution.

extra.message: In course_xml_fold_735, attacker-supplied request body is parsed by lxml with etree.XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False). cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: In course_mongo_lane_711, the JSON request body (or its 'filter' field) is passed directly as the MongoDB query to find_one() without any validation or operator filtering. An attacker can inject NoSQL operators such as {'$ne': null} or {'$regex': '.*'} to bypass intended query semantics and exfiltrate arbitrary records from the ops.records collection.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Used in a NoSQL Database Query

extra.message: In course_vault_stash_250, the user-supplied GET parameter 'ref' is interpolated directly into a filesystem path: target = BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json". There is no sanitization, so payloads like ref=../../etc/cron.d/evil (with target.parent.mkdir(parents=True) creating directories as needed) write files outside the intended private_exports directory, allowing arbitrary file write on the server.

extra.message: The public SignUpForm exposes a user-selectable 'role' ChoiceField using User.ROLE_CHOICES (including 'school_admin' and 'instructor'), and 'role' is listed in Meta.fields. extra.message: The file_upload view creates the Resource via Resource.objects.create(file=file, ...). Django model validators (the FileExtensionValidator restricting uploads to pdf/docx/pptx/mp4/zip/csv/xlsx/txt defined on Resource.file in core/models.py:154-157) only run during full_clean(), which objects.create() bypasses. Users can therefore upload files of any type (e.g. .html or .svg containing scripts). Because lms/urls.py serves MEDIA_ROOT inline via static() when DEBUG is on, a victim opening the uploaded file URL yields stored cross-site scripting.

extra.message: In export_grades, csv.writer writes user-controlled values directly into the exported CSV: sub.student.display_name() (first/last name editable by the student via ProfileForm) and grade.feedback. Values beginning with '=', '+', '-', or '@' are interpreted as formulas by Excel/LibreOffice when the exported grades file is opened, enabling CSV/formula injection (e.g. =HYPERLINK("http://evil/","click") or =cmd|'/c calc'!A1) against instructors and admins.

extra.message: In export_submissions_report, csv.writer writes user-controlled fields (student display_name, which any user can set via the profile form) directly into the CSV export without neutralizing formula characters. When a school admin opens the report in a spreadsheet application, values starting with '=', '+', '-', or '@' execute as formulas (CSV injection), which can be used to exfiltrate data or execute commands via DDE payloads.

extra.message: SECRET_KEY falls back to the hardcoded value 'django-insecure-local-dev-only' when the environment variable is not set. There is no fail-safe that prevents startup in production with the default key.
